## Example 3.1 {#dc3-example-3-1-sin .dc-lesson .dc-graph-lesson}

<p class="dc-graph-intro">The derivative of a function can be explored graphically by analysing its gradients at specific points.</p><div class="dc-graph-prompts"><p><strong>a)</strong> Estimate the gradient of the tangent to $y=\sin x$ at $x=0,\frac\pi2,\pi,\frac{3\pi}2,2\pi$ and record these in the table below.</p><p><strong>b)</strong> Plot these gradient values on a blank set of axes and connect them to sketch the derivative graph.</p></div><div class="dc-trig-graph" data-dc-trig="sin">
<svg class="dc-trig-svg" viewBox="0 0 1140 265" role="img" aria-label="sin graph with movable tangent and axes for its derivative graph"></svg>
<div class="dc-graph-controls"><label><span data-math="x"></span><input type="range" min="0" max="1000" value="0" aria-label="Tangent position on sin graph"></label><button data-position="0.0" aria-pressed="true"><span data-math="0"></span></button><button data-position="0.25" aria-pressed="false"><span data-math="\frac\pi2"></span></button><button data-position="0.5" aria-pressed="false"><span data-math="\pi"></span></button><button data-position="0.75" aria-pressed="false"><span data-math="\frac{3\pi}2"></span></button><button data-position="1.0" aria-pressed="false"><span data-math="2\pi"></span></button></div>
<table class="dc-gradient-table"><thead><tr><th><span data-math="x"></span></th><th><span data-math="0"></span></th><th><span data-math="\frac\pi2"></span></th><th><span data-math="\pi"></span></th><th><span data-math="\frac{3\pi}2"></span></th><th><span data-math="2\pi"></span></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th>Gradient of <span data-math="y=\sin x"></span></th><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="1"></span></span></td><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="0"></span></span></td><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="-1"></span></span></td><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="0"></span></span></td><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="1"></span></span></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p class="fragment dc-graph-result" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x)=\cos x"></span></p></div><p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 16 · Example 3.1(a–b, d)</p>

::: notes
Booklet Example 3.1: (a)–(b). The exact five angles and gradient values are retained. Move the tangent using the slider or angle buttons. The graph uses equal horizontal and vertical unit scales, so the tangent angle represents its gradient faithfully. Students estimate and record the gradients first; the right-hand axes and table are deliberately blank. Next reveals the completed table, linked derivative curve and derivative rule simultaneously. Previous hides them together. The derivative graph includes the five recorded points and the current gradient point; its values agree with the slope of the tangent on the left. Gradients: 1, 0, -1, 0, 1. Match cosine. This local graphing application supports part (d); five sample points alone do not prove the rule for every x. The plotted derivative is the exact derivative curve, providing an informal graphical verification rather than a formal proof. Radians are essential. Allow about five minutes across both slides.
:::
